sample_unit: oncology decision points (1,586 NCCN guideline items and 419 colorectal cancer case items)
models_evaluated: nine frontier LLMs (four closed-source, five open-weight families)

links.outcome: Share of oncology guideline and case items answered correctly by none of nine LLMs
links.effect: 42.1% (Wilson 95% CI 40.0%–44.3%) of all items were answered correctly by none; 35.7% of 1,586 NCCN guideline items and 66.4% of 419 colorectal cancer case items.
links.quote: Treating the nine as a pooled super-model, 42.1% (Wilson 95% CI40.0%–44.3%) of all items—35.7% of the 1,586 NCCN guideline items and 66.4%of the 419 colorectal cancer case items—were answered correctly by none;

links.outcome: Unsafe commitments versus cautious deferral among LLMs on oncology decision points
links.effect: Two decisiveness-tuned models made unsafe commitments three to five times more often than the seven cautious models without scoring higher overall.
links.quote: Two models tuned for decisiveness (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview) made unsafe commitments between three andfive times more often than the seven cautious models without scoring higheroverall—in our sample, agentic tuning did not consistently yield netimprovement.

unlisted_practices: Using a deterministic, zero-LLM-inference scorer to classify clinical failure types in LLM benchmark outputs
Pooling multiple LLMs (ensembles) to compensate for individual model blind spots

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating frontier LLMs on clinical decision points (guideline-conformant oncology reasoning and case-specific tasks) using an automated deterministic scorer without testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
